concept: Monochrome table portrait with cosmic details
creativeDirection: Studio portrait photography: rebuild the sparse table-and-wall geometry of source 2 as a controlled set, then fold in a few tactile motifs from the other sleeves as real props and painted details while keeping the scene readable as one crisp photograph.
scene: A purpose-built studio set with a textured pale wall, a simple rectangular table, mismatched chairs, and an opening at the right suggesting the spare interior from source 2. Three women sit and lean around the table in the poised arrangement of source 2, photographed front-on. The set is mostly monochrome, but a few carefully placed accents bring in this week's other records: a small dark doll with pale hair stands on the tabletop, a simple cat face is painted small on an olive chair seat, and a suspended saucer-shaped practical light above the table casts a faint geometric beam shape onto the wall. The mood is formal, strange, and clean rather than theatrical.

elements.element: the three women from reference image 2 posed around a table in coordinated formal outfits, within a sparse textured-wall studio set based on that sleeve
the small dark doll-like figure with light hair placed on the table as a real object
a saucer-shaped overhead lamp with a subtle beam-like patch of light on the wall
a small stylized cat face painted on the olive seat of one chair
warm amber-black accents in small studio equipment details and shadows
muted gold and blue notes in the metallic fixtures and cool edge highlights
tiny restrained touches of red and blue in the otherwise neutral scene

prompt: A face-on seated group portrait in a purpose-built studio set, framed medium-wide at eye level with little depth; a sparse textured pale wall, a simple rectangular table, mismatched chairs, and an opening at the right recreate the minimal interior geometry of reference image 2. The three women from reference image 2 are the primary subject, posed seated and leaning around the table in their coordinated formal outfits, looking toward the camera with composed expressions, preserving their arrangement and styling. On the tabletop, include the small dark doll-like figure with light hair from reference image 1 as a real object; above the table, a saucer-shaped practical lamp inspired by reference image 5 casts a subtle beam-like geometric patch onto the wall; on the seat of one olive chair, paint a small stylized cat face from reference image 7. Let reference image 4 influence a few amber-black studio hardware details and shadow tones, reference image 6 influence restrained gold metal notes and faint cool blue edge highlights, and reference image 3 contribute only tiny accents of red and blue within the otherwise neutral set. Crisp studio portrait photography, physically plausible set build, clean editorial realism, no collage look. Balanced asymmetry, clear visual hierarchy on the three women, faces fully legible, sharp focus, cool skylight-style key with soft fill, gentle shadow definition, no murk. Palette of black, white, gray, cream, olive, amber, muted gold, and cool blue; mood poised, uncanny, elegant. Reference map for people (the album images are attached in this numbered order): reference image 2 shows three women seated and leaning around a table in coordinated outfits, and reference images 9, 10, 11 are enlarged close-ups of those same people, one face each from left to right - take each face from its own close-up. Copy each of these faces directly from that numbered reference image - same face, bone structure, hair, expression, and styling - rather than drawing a new person from the description. Nobody from reference images 1, 3 appears in the picture: use those images only for colour, setting, and objects, and add no figures, faces, or silhouettes from them. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails, posters, record covers, or pictures on a screen, monitor, or television. A sleeve's abstract graphics, shapes, patterns, and colours may be painted onto the walls, doors, floor, or objects of the place as part of its decoration, without any lettering. Show no sleeve's faces, heads, or figures as a picture, mural, display, sign, relief, or silhouette anywhere; transform the sleeves' non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling, and their apparent age: every person is shown as the adult they are on the sleeve, never younger, smoothed, or more boyish or girlish. Keep each reference person in the pose, expression, and gaze the sleeve shows, and keep every identifiable face sharp, lit, unobscured, and in focus: no motion blur, long-exposure smearing, steam, fog, shadow, crowding, or shallow depth of field over a reference person's face. Expose the image cleanly whatever the light: every person's face well lit and readable, shadows that hold detail, and clear colour, with no murky underexposure, crushed blacks, heavy film grain, digital noise, or dust-and-scratches texture. Add no incidental plants: no flowers, potted plants, planters, climbing vines, ivy, hanging foliage, hedges, lawns, flower beds, or greenery framing the edges or carpeting the floor, unless the description above explicitly asks for that plant as part of a source motif or the year treatment. Dress the scene with the materials of the place itself - stone, metal, concrete, wood, fabric, glass, water, equipment - rather than vegetation. Everyone in the picture is photographed in the same place, at the same moment, under the same light as the rest of the scene, in full colour and with the same lens and grain: do not carry over a sleeve's own backdrop, studio lighting, backlit flare, monochrome, colour cast, or print texture onto the person. Each person stands inside the scene at the scale of the space around them, never as an oversized cropped head or bust looming at the edge of the frame over a distant scene, and never washed in red, blue, or other coloured light. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere. The only people anywhere in the image are the reference people named in the reference map, and of those only the ones whose faces are clearly visible in their reference. Add no one else: no extra band members, musicians, staff, bystanders, passers-by, crowd, audience, background or out-of-focus figures, and no hands, arms, legs, or shadows of unseen people. Never complete a person who is hidden, cropped, turned away, blurred, or only partly visible in a reference with an invented face or body - leave that person out entirely. Photograph the reference people from roughly eye level, at three-quarter length or closer, in the near or middle ground, so each of their faces is large, sharp, and clearly recognisable in the final frame: never from directly above, and never as small distant figures.
